loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.

separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.

view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.

shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating transient intent from persistent preferences with adaptive fusion. [TLSTSRec (online 2024; volume 2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) combines long- and short-term temporal information through trainable timestamp representations and personalized fusion layers. [Multi-Scale Transformers (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) uses dual attention for transient and stable interests, with adaptive masking to reduce redundant interactions. Earlier, directly relevant [TLSRec (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) introduced time-lag-sensitive fusion of hierarchical long- and short-term preferences. These provide architectural precedents; they do not establish gains on the four pinned Amazon categories.

Practical hypothesis for SASRec: retain its causal sequence representation, add a recent-window branch and a pooled historical-preference branch, then learn a sigmoid gate conditioned on both representations, observed inter-event gaps and history length. A small learned decay over log-scaled elapsed times is a reasonable ablation, rather than an established result from these papers. [TSAPE (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3774904.3792333) offers another lightweight direction: adaptive temporal positional encoding integrated into SASRec. For sparse histories, compare gating against simple pooling and fixed mixtures to determine whether added parameters help. Compute every temporal feature from the available history prefix; without a known prediction timestamp, anchor elapsed times to its latest interaction. Select using the unchanged macro validation HR@10. Interaction timing supports relevance modeling, but does not establish ownership, replacement needs or unobserved user traits.

---

Replacing single-negative BCE is well motivated, but no sampling strategy consistently wins. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses partly to negative-sampling-induced overconfidence; its underlying method combines more negatives with calibrated gBCE. A [2024 sequential-recommendation comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), covering random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling, finds dataset-dependent tradeoffs: random sampling favors head items, while popularity-based methods can balance popularity bands at some cost to aggregate accuracy. These results justify controlled comparisons, not an assumed Electronics improvement.

Popularity correction must match the actual sampler. [Sampled-softmax derivation](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf) subtracts log sampling probability or expected count from training logits; a uniform/popularity mixture therefore needs its mixture distribution, rather than popularity alone. Deterministic top-score mining does not automatically provide valid sampling probabilities. Hard negatives also risk suppressing genuinely relevant unobserved items: [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses this using teacher-generated soft labels and consistency regularization. This is supporting older evidence, not a verified 2024–2026 breakthrough.

Practical inference for this benchmark: compare uniform multi-negative softmax, multi-negative gBCE, then a modest uniform/hard mixture with a warm-up. Mask padding, target collisions and observed training positives; treat remaining false negatives as unresolved. Tune negative count, temperature and hard fraction within the shared GPU budget, selecting exclusively by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Weak sampled margins are a hypothesis generator, not validation evidence.

---

Recent work supports modeling directed associations separately from semantic similarity. [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/transitivity-encoded-graph-attention-networks-for-complementary-item-recommendations) encodes behavioral direction and couples complementary/substitute graphs, addressing noisy, sparse co-purchases. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09209v1) offers a lightweight alternative: project user–item interactions into weighted item links, then adjust direction using inverse-distance-weighted purchase order within short windows. Important limitation: its sparsity treatment uses item-category transitions, unavailable here; reported improvements do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

Content–sequence hybrids provide architectural inspiration, but pretrained semantics often supply their advantage. [SAGERec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/24/4844) combines a sparse semantic graph, adaptive edge weighting and a Transformer, explicitly relying on LLM embeddings. [AlleCompanion (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063) filters co-purchase noise through category constraints, expert feedback and LLM reasoning. Neither transfers directly under the available-data and no-pretrained-weights constraints.

A plausible experiment—not an established result—is SASRec plus a sparse directed transition-score residual, with separate source/target embeddings and a small title/description encoder trained from scratch. Use lexical features or pooled trainable token embeddings to share information across sparse items; tune graph/content contributions through macro validation HR@10 and ablate each branch. Interpret learned edges as predictive associations: temporal order and textual resemblance do not establish functional complementarity, substitution or exact compatibility. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses positive next items and sampled negatives. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
